subject: Helios dedicated capacity intake — pool sizing, burst SLA, and netops next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya@helios.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro: Helios dedicated capacity intake & next steps

Hi team — looping you all in for Helios' Dedicated capacity intake. Maya, great to meet you — thanks for filling out the intake form (attached). High level from Helios: they want predictable throughput for their document-parsing service with occasional nightly batch jobs and an expected marketing-driven spike around product launches. Key asks from the call:

- Target steady-state QPS: ~180 requests/sec (median), peak bursts up to ~450 req/sec for ~20–30min windows.
- Latency SLO: p99 <= 240ms for short responses; longer tails acceptable for batch jobs.
- Regions: primary in us-west-2, DR in eu-west-1; may later expand to ap-southeast-1.
- Data residency: model inputs contain pseudonymized PII — standard Private deployment controls are required.

What we need from implementation: initial pool sizing (GPU type & count), autoscale/burst proposal (how much warm standby, cold-start time), netops/regional cross-connect requests (Samir on their side), and a simple mutual action plan (MAP) with dates so procurement can align.

Attachments: Helios_intake_form.xlsx (filled)

Next steps I propose: 1) Irene to review intake & propose MAP draft, 2) Priyom to propose a recommended pool config and warm-standby/burst approach, 3) Ben to coordinate procurement timelines and commitment thresholds.

Maya — can you confirm target go-live quarter (Q3/Q4)? Also please include Samir from your netops if he needs to approve cross-connects.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa — quick read of the intake looks good. I sketched a first-pass MAP and added as a lightweight PDF (redwood_map_draft.pdf) — link below — but main asks / clarifications before we finalize:

1) Burst behavior: do they expect predictable scheduled bursts (e.g., marketing sends at known times) or stochastic bursts (unpredictable, customer-triggered)? Scheduled bursts let us pre-warm capacity for much lower risk.
2) SLA/credits tolerance: will Helios require formal uptime/latency credits for Dedicated, or is a best-effort with canary fallback acceptable for initial quarters?
3) Netops: Samir will need to provide IP blocks and confirm peering/cross-connect window. If cross-connect lead time is >10 business days we may need to provision in a different subnet and route via a vpn for initial testing.

Proposed MAP (high-level milestones):
- Day 0–3: Intake review & finalize pool sizing
- Day 4–10: Netops handshake + procurement signoff (Ben)
- Day 11–20: Capacity provisioning + kernel selection & quantization profile (Priyom)
- Day 21–25: Canary routing + smoke tests (CS + SRE)
- Day 26–30: Cutover / go-live window

Priyom — can you attach a short config matrix for GPU type, per-GPU QPS estimate, and warm-standby recommendation? Ben — can you call out any procurement lead-times we should bake into the MAP? Maya — if you can confirm whether bursts are scheduled that will change the warm-standby sizing.

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cHeliosOnboard

Thanks,
Irene

Subject: Re: Intro: Helios dedicated capacity intake & next steps — proposed config

Thanks — I put together a short technical recommendation and a ballpark cost estimate (capacity_estimate_20290613.pdf attached). TL;DR recommendation: start with a primary pool sized for steady-state and a small warm-burst pool that can be hot-swapped in under 60s. Details: 

- Primary: 8x A100-80GB (NVLink), target steady QPS handling ~180 req/sec with p99 ~180–220ms using moderate batching and prefix caching.
- Warm-burst pool: 4x A100-80GB kept as hot standby with minimal active containers to allow instant scale-in/out; target activation time < 60s when we flip routing.
- Autoscale policy: target GPU utilization 65% (avg across pool), scale up step +2 GPUs, scale down step -1 GPU with 120s cooldown. For scheduled bursts we recommend pre-warm rules: for known windows (cron) scale to N+X 15 minutes before event.
- Batch sizing & kernels: recommend adaptive batching with max batch 64 for parsing pipelines, KV cache sized to ~3GB per model for typical session lengths.
- Quantization: 8-bit dynamic where acceptable to reduce memory pressure; Priyom can finalize based on the model repo.
- Network/regional notes: primary in us-west-2. If netops lead-time is long, provision a temporary vpn-backed test subnet to validate routing while cross-connect is provisioned.

Estimated monthly cost (reserved + some burst buffer): ballpark $xxk–$yyk depending on reserved commit. See attached PDF for numbers and assumptions.

Attachments: capacity_estimate_20290613.pdf

Action items I own: produce final kernel/quant profile after model import (ETA 5 business days once model artifacts are available).
